notes:
### New

- Lets agents message Cursor, TRAE, WorkBuddy, ZCode, Qoder and Kimi Code sessions, and lets those sessions message others. Turn it on in Settings → Agent plugins → Agent tools → Let agents message each other; Settings → Agent plugins has a HUD tools row for each of them.
  - A message reaches one of these sessions through the client's own completion hook, so it goes in when the session's turn ends and the session carries on with it. An idle session takes it at the end of its next turn. Only an interactive Qoder CLI session takes a message while idle.
  - A client carries a turn on only a few times in a row (Cursor and TRAE 4, ZCode, WorkBuddy and Qoder 3, Kimi Code 1); more messages wait for a later turn. A message nobody took within an hour expires.
  - TRAE runs hooks only after you turn them on in TRAE's Settings → Hooks. WorkBuddy starts Agent HUD's tools only after you trust the connector under Connectors → Custom connectors and switch it on.
  - Kimi Code gets Agent HUD's hooks for this, in its `config.toml`. Requests from Kimi Code are still not answered from the HUD.
  - The paper plane flies for these sessions too, and the sender can read the answer once the turn ends.
- Lets Pi and OpenCode sessions take and send agent messages. An open session takes a waiting message once it is idle, and a message that comes during a turn waits for its end. Agent HUD adds its tools to Pi's `mcp.json` and to OpenCode's `opencode.json`. This works with OpenCode 1; OpenCode 2, Oh My Pi, Kilo Code and MiMo Code don't take messages yet.
- Adds switches for each screen in Settings → Display, under On this screen: Show the HUD on this screen, and under it Messages, Requests and Agent messages in flight. A screen with the HUD off shows nothing, cards included; the other three hide the message cards and the tail, the request cards and the head, or the paper plane. Agents can't change these through the HUD tools, and Reset leaves them alone.
- Draws the hover panel as cards. Each block and each section has a ground and a frame of its own, in place of the lines between them. Cards side by side stand at one height, and the token chart fills its card. A panel styled without separators looks as it did.
- Counts Agent HUD Remote's seats as one pool. App Store subscriptions and license keys add up, and the computers turned on most recently hold the seats.
  - A computer beyond the seats turns its own Remote off; turn it on again once a seat is free. With no valid purchase every computer pauses and comes back by itself.
  - A Mac that was off for a month no longer takes its seat back from the computer that took it meanwhile.
  - The Subscription and Remote pages speak of computers. My computers lists every other computer using a seat, with its platform and whether it is within the paid seats.
- Reads these agents more closely:
  - TRAE's quota is counted as TRAE's own app counts it, and WorkBuddy's credits show as a balance, "Available credits" in Statistics. TRAE's, WorkBuddy's and Qoder's quotas come only from the sign-in you make in Agent HUD's own window.
  - Kimi Code shows its account and plan, its sessions' titles and its archived sessions.
  - ZCode's sessions follow its renames, archive and sub-agents, and its conversations can be read.
  - A Qoder session is titled by what you first typed, and names its model.
- Adds How agent messages work → Open the guide to Settings → Agent plugins → Agent tools (#56, #59).

### Fixes

- Stops the steady CPU use while Antigravity runs (#53). A large conversation that Antigravity kept writing to was read again from its first row every two seconds, and the read never finished. A change is now read from where the last read stopped: about 1% CPU in place of 7 to 8% on a 155 MB conversation written every 20 seconds, and nothing once the writing stops.
- Shows DeepSeek's balance for Pi on a DeepSeek API key (#64). Pi's tokens showed without a balance. The balance's currency now also picks the price list for Pi's DeepSeek tokens.
- Asks a sending agent for one whole message (#54). Each message is a turn of its own for the receiver, so three partial messages about one task made it review the work three times.
- Shows a Cursor chat as running while its turn goes on. Only Cursor's completion hook was installed, so a chat never showed running.
- Reads the 30 days of usage shared with the iPhone at most every 30 seconds. It was read again each time new usage came in while your history was still being read, and always on a computer that shares over the local network only, which cost CPU each time.
- Sends an agent's waiting message into a Claude Code session it started before that session moves into the Claude desktop app.
- Scrolls the hover panel without scroll bars. A dark bar flashed along its side and bottom while the panel grew.
